question: According to standard clinical definitions, infertility is the failure to achieve a clinical pregnancy after how many months of regular, unprotected sexual intercourse in women aged 35 years or younger?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Six months applies when the woman is older than 35 years, or when there are known risk factors. For women ≤35, the standard threshold is 12 months.
Correct. The standard definition is 12 months of regular, unprotected intercourse. For women >35 years, investigation is appropriate after 6 months due to declining ovarian reserve.
Eighteen months is not a recognised clinical threshold for defining infertility.
Twenty-four months is too long. The 12-month (or 6-month for >35) threshold exists so that evaluation can begin while treatment options remain maximally effective.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the definition of infertility: 12 months for women ≤35, and 6 months for women >35 or those with known risk factors.
Well done. The 12-month rule for women ≤35 is the foundation of the infertility definition; recognising the 6-month exception for older women shows clinical precision.
